title: R5 residence districts - maximum residential floor area ratio (standard zoning lots)
description: DRAFT extraction (needs_review) of the maximum residential floor area ratio for standard zoning lots in R5, R5A, R5B and R5D districts, per NYC Zoning Resolution section 23-21. NOT a Verified determination: it is a candidate representation awaiting raw-HTML source verification and G6 qualified-human legal approval. The engine computes the standard-zoning-lot FAR and the resulting maximum residential floor area from the lot area; the higher 'qualifying residential sites' FAR is surfaced as a conditional alternative rather than silently applied or ignored. The ZR 23-21 footnote-1 0.60 single-dwelling-unit equivalent-FAR cap does NOT apply to the R5 family: the byte-verified recapture (commit 17e8eb78) proved footnote 1 is scoped to the first table row's standard value only (R1/R2/R3), so this rule no longer carries it - it is attached to r1-r2-r3-residential-far instead, keeping the whole R1-R12 family consistent with one source reading. effective_from is the section's Last Amended date (2024-12-05): evaluating as_of a date before it yields a visible not-effective outcome rather than applying today's values to a period this draft does not represent.

citations.quote: In the districts indicated, the maximum residential floor area ratio shall be as set forth in the following table. Separate maximum residential floor area ratios are set forth for standard zoning lots and zoning lots that are qualifying residential sites.

inputs.name: zoning_district
inputs.description: The residence district governing the lot (or the portion under evaluation). District SCOPE is enforced by applicability (in_set R5/R5A/R5B/R5D), NOT by an input domain enum: a non-R5 district is a visible not_applicable, never an invalid input. Must be a confident, non-collapsed assignment; an uncertain M2-T013 geometric assignment is passed via spatial_context and downgrades coverage.

inputs.name: lot_area_sq_ft
inputs.description: Zoning-lot area in square feet; must be strictly positive. A zero/negative/non-finite value is rejected fail-closed (professional_review_required, no computed value) so the engine never produces a bogus (negative/NaN/inf) floor area.

inputs.name: site_class
inputs.description: Whether the lot is a standard zoning lot or a 'qualifying residential site'. When absent, the qualifying-site alternative is surfaced as conditional (not decided).

outputs.name: max_residential_far
outputs.description: Maximum residential floor area ratio for a standard zoning lot in the district.

outputs.name: max_residential_floor_area_sq_ft
outputs.description: Maximum residential floor area = lot area x FAR.

parameters.name: standard_far_by_district
parameters.note: Standard-zoning-lot maximum residential FAR by district from the ZR 23-21 table (R5/R5A/R5B = 1.50; R5D = 2.00). Candidate values pending raw-HTML verification and G6 approval.

parameters.name: qualifying_far_by_district
parameters.note: Qualifying-residential-sites maximum residential FAR (ZR 23-21 second column) for the R5 rows: 2.00 for R5, R5A, R5B and R5D. SURFACED as the conditional alternative (see the qualifying_residential_site exception), never applied by this rule: whether a lot is a qualifying residential site is a separate legal determination. Provenance-linked here so the material alternative is byte-checkable against the snapshot; deliberately not consumed by a computation step, so the standard value stays the only computed result and no R5 standard FAR value changes.

steps.note: Select the standard-zoning-lot maximum residential FAR for the district (ZR 23-21 table).
Maximum residential floor area = lot area (sq ft) x FAR.

exceptions.description: A higher maximum residential FAR - the qualifying-residential-sites value 2.00 for R5, R5A, R5B and R5D per ZR 23-21 (see the qualifying_far_by_district parameter) - applies to zoning lots that are 'qualifying residential sites'. Whether a specific lot qualifies is a separate legal determination and is not decided by this rule; when the site class is unknown or qualifying, the result is conditional and the higher FAR may apply.
exceptions.note: Surfaced, never collapsed: the standard-lot FAR is reported with an explicit conditional flag that a qualifying-site FAR may govern.

special_district_interactions.description: Special Purpose Districts (ZR Articles VIII-XIV) and other mapped overlays may modify residence-district floor area. When a mapped special district applies, its provisions govern and must be evaluated by the corresponding special rule; this general rule does not apply the modification.

uncertainty_policy.note: An uncertain, split, sliver, or invalid M2-T013 geometric district assignment is never collapsed into a single definitive district: coverage is downgraded to professional_review_required (or data_conflict) and the geometric uncertainty is recorded in the trace.

limitations: Draft extraction pending raw-HTML source verification and G6 qualified-human legal approval; not a Verified determination.

Only the standard-zoning-lot residential FAR is computed; the qualifying-residential-site FAR is surfaced (conditional), not computed. The ZR 23-21 footnote-1 0.60 single-dwelling-unit equivalent-FAR cap does not apply to the R5 family and is intentionally absent (it is attached to r1-r2-r3-residential-far).
Special Purpose District and other overlay modifications are not applied.
